_why: The committed floor for scripts/check_impl_mapping.py's MIN_MAPPINGS.
MIN_MAPPINGS is the only protection the Implementation Mapping tables
have, and it lives in the same file an author editing a guide is
already editing: lowering a pin and deleting the rows left the gate
green and all of TestImplementationMappingGate green with it. The
comment above MIN_MAPPINGS says 'never lower one to make CI pass',
which is a convention and not a check (audit_040_r2/gates, finding G6).
MIN_MAPPINGS[path] >= floor[path], so lowering a pin now takes an edit
to two files in opposite directions instead of one number in one file.
Raising a pin needs no change here. Lowering one -- which should be
rare and deliberate -- means a guide legitimately shrank, and the
reason belongs in the commit message that lowers both.
